Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Receive budgets preserve complete packets

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Client and server pumps pass only their remaining byte allowance to transport.receive. If the next complete packet does not fit, the transport returns Buffer_Too_Small and retains it. The pump stops and tries again with a fresh allowance next time. An exactly exhausted budget stops before another read. Packet count and byte limits are unchanged.

Before the receive-budget fix, loops read into the full 64 KiB buffer and checked the budget only after dequeueing. The crossing packet was then discarded, even on a reliable channel. Reliability cannot recover a packet already accepted and removed from the transport's receive queue. Large actions could stall until application retry; large fact batches could leave observer event history incomplete.

Every legal packet fits a fresh pump: transport.MAX_PACKET_BYTES is 65,536, and network configuration already requires bytes_per_pump >= 65,536. This uses the existing receive-retention contract and existing buffers, queue bounds, byte budgets and retry paths. Buffer_Too_Small is not a malformed-packet rejection. Authority traffic counters still count successfully received authority packets; client traffic from other senders consumes the work budget before being rejected, without being attributed to the authority.

All transport adapters must retain data on a short destination, including wrappers. Their bounded internal polling/queues remain separate from the application's per-pump dispatch allowance. A retained packet still undergoes the usual scope, generation, epoch, admission and content checks when received. This change does not promise delivery across a disconnected or expired binding.

The regression suite uses authentic generated protocol packets. At the minimum byte budget, three large fact batches previously yielded only 32 of 96 observer effects; now all 96 arrive once. Two large action submissions previously applied only the first; now both apply without any additional client pump or resend. Each pump stays within its byte budget. Unknown senders and exact exhaustion are also checked. Real ENet and Chrome RTC probes exercise short-buffer retention, metadata/payload integrity, both channels, replacement and adapter restart.

This independent defect was found while investigating the older Claimball C2 observer-effect failure. The historical failure has no captured delivery schedule, and its cause remains unestablished. A current fault run with complete effects and strict replay is a regression check, not retrospective proof of that cause.
